newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Maybank, Rashid, seen up on bank deal.
newsitem.headline: Maybank, Rashid, seen up on bank deal.

text.p: Shares of Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) and stockbroker Rashid Hussain Bhd are expected to rise at their requotation on Monday following news of a 2.16 billion ringgit bank merger, dealers said.
Last week, Rashid Hussain and Maybank, Malaysia's largest commercial bank, signed a deal in which Rashid acquired 75 percent of the equity in Maybank's Kwong Yik Bank Bhd for 8.80 ringgit a share.
Under the deal, Kwong Yik will be merged with Rahid's 20- percent owned DCB Holdings Bhd banking unit, DCB Bank Bhd.
All four company stocks have been suspended since late October for the news announcement.
"They (the banking stocks) should be up," said a dealer with a local securities firm. "Kwong Yik should go up at least to 8.80 ringgit."

Dealers said the gray, or off-market, price being quoted for Rashid's stock was between 18.00 ringgit and 21.00 ringgit a share. Rashid, which runs Malaysia's largest institutional stockbroker, closed at 15.80 ringgit on October 18.
A banking analyst with a local research house said Maybank's stock could rise as high as 26.40 ringgit from its 25 ringgit close on October 18.
Kwong Yik's stock should move in tandem with DCB, as both companies are being merged, she said. Kwong Yik's shares closed at 6.95 ringgit while DCB ended at 8.65 ringgit on October 18.
